evidenceAudit.scope: Adults listed for elective abdominal wall hernia repair (e.g. inguinal): urgent features, NICE NG45 pre-operative tests for intermediate surgery, VTE and antibiotic prophylaxis. Verified against NICE NG45 (primary inguinal hernia repair is its example of intermediate surgery), NG180, NG89 and Saudi MOH Protocol-015 (hernioplasty/mesh). No hernia-specific Saudi or NICE guideline was found.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 12 Oct 2026.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: No hernia-specific guideline (e.g. HerniaSurge) opened in this run
SFDA registration not checked per drug
Local antibiogram may add gentamicin (MOH p. 1)

pathophysiology.summary: A hernia is protrusion of abdominal contents through a defect in the abdominal wall. Inguinal hernias are most common. Risk is from incarceration and strangulation, when blood supply to the trapped bowel is compromised.
keyMechanisms: Raised intra-abdominal pressure (coughing, straining, lifting) pushes contents through a weak area or defect.
A narrow neck traps contents (incarceration); venous then arterial compromise causes strangulation and ischaemia.
Mesh repair reinforces the defect — mesh is a foreign body, so antibiotic prophylaxis applies (MOH).

symptoms: Groin or abdominal-wall lump, larger on standing or coughing.
redFlags: Irreducible, tender lump — incarceration/strangulation: urgent surgical review
Vomiting, distension, absent flatus — bowel obstruction

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Below and lateral to pubic tubercle; higher strangulation risk.

clinicalManagement.title: Listing
actions: Primary inguinal hernia repair is graded intermediate surgery for test selection (NICE NG45).
Urgent rather than elective repair if irreducible, tender or obstructed.

clinicalManagement.title: Pre-operative assessment
actions: Grade surgery (minor, intermediate, major/complex) and ASA status; order only the tests NICE NG45 lists for that combination.
Do not routinely order chest X-ray, urine dipstick, sickle tests or HbA1c in people without diabetes (NICE NG45).
Discuss stopping smoking and reducing alcohol; manage iron-deficiency anaemia (NICE NG180).
Make an individual anticoagulant plan if the person takes anticoagulants (NICE NG45).

clinicalManagement.title: VTE prophylaxis
actions: Mechanical prophylaxis from admission until mobile; add LMWH for at least 7 days if VTE risk outweighs bleeding risk (NICE NG89 1.14 abdominal surgery).

clinicalManagement.title: Surgical antibiotic prophylaxis (MOH Protocol-015)
actions: Hernioplasty/herniorrhaphy or mesh placement: cefazolin 2 g IV (3 g if 120 kg or more) within 60 min of incision (MOH p. 3).
Allergy: clindamycin 900 mg IV (60 min) or vancomycin 15 mg/kg (max 2 g) IV within 120 min (MOH p. 3).
Re-dose cefazolin every 4 h (or clindamycin every 6 h) if surgery lasts more than 4 h or blood loss exceeds 1,500 mL (MOH p. 1).
Stop prophylaxis within 24 h of the end of surgery, even with drains or catheters (MOH p. 4).

keyPoints: Exclude strangulation — irreducible tender hernia is urgent.
pitfalls: Listing an irreducible tender hernia as elective.
Routine bloods in fit young patients (ASA 1).

patientEducation: Avoid heavy lifting per surgeon's advice; return for a painful irreducible lump.
lifestyleAndDiet: Stop smoking and reduce alcohol before surgery (NICE NG180).
Stay active; prehabilitation exercises where advised.
dischargeCriteria: Pain controlled with oral analgesia; eating, drinking and mobilising.
Wound satisfactory; VTE prophylaxis plan and follow-up arranged.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Post-operative review per surgical team; return immediately with fever, wound redness, calf swelling, breathlessness or chest pain.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Primary inguinal hernia repair = intermediate (NICE NG45)
